admission.justification: Cancel-and-restart was weighed and rejected because it cannot continue a half-published generation; future recovery controls must preserve the accepted identity rather than strand or replace it.

alternatives.option: Admit public recover on the accepted doorless direct record and settle its kept receipt in that call.
alternatives.reason: The existing executor can continue the same generation; dispatch need not invent a closeout door.

alternatives.option: Treat cancel and a fresh direct landing as the continuation route and retain public recover refusal.
alternatives.reason: Cancel abandons rather than continues the accepted generation and is unavailable once a leg has moved.
alternatives.reconsider_when: An explicitly approved replacement protocol can continue an already partly published direct generation without losing its recorded authority or history.

consequences: Direct dispatch bypasses ordinary closeout door checks only on its admitted direct record.
Ordinary closeout records without task intent keep their existing treatment.
Proof must distinguish same-generation public completion and receipt settlement from executor-only success.
context: Missing task intent stripped public recover from direct records, while cancel was available only before either leg changed, stranding a code-first interrupted publication.
